projectName: Summit Line Roofing — Marketing Site (synthetic pilot)
goal: A multi-section marketing site for a small local roofing and gutter company (fictional). It must explain plainly what the company does, show the three service packages and how a job runs, show clearly labelled SAMPLE customer feedback, answer common questions, and give homeowners one clear way to request a free roof inspection. Required sections, in order: hero, services, packages, process, proof, faq, contact. SYNTHETIC PROVISIONAL BRIEF written 2026-09-30: the client, its business facts and its request are fictional and are not a real client or Nick's brief.
brandNotes: Tone: plain-spoken, calm, trustworthy, practical; a tradesperson explaining things to a neighbour, not a sales pitch. Short sentences, no hype, no exclamation marks, no emoji. Style direction: deep pine green (#1F3D36) and warm cream (#F6F1E7) with one copper accent (#B5642A) for buttons and links; a sturdy sans-serif for headings and a highly readable body face; generous spacing; real-feeling layout, not a generic template. Use no photographs of people and no stock imagery presented as the company's own work; simple line illustrations or CSS shapes only. Accessibility: aim for WCAG 2.2 AA (contrast at least 4.5:1 for body text, visible keyboard focus, a working skip link, one h1, logical heading order, labelled form fields, tap targets at least 44px, respects prefers-reduced-motion). Performance: single self-contained page, no third-party scripts or web-font requests, images (if any) sized and lazy-loaded, target LCP under 2.5 s on a mid-range phone; must read well from 360px wide upward. Contact: one primary call to action, 'Request a free roof inspection', which opens a short form (name, phone, address or suburb, what you need, preferred time of day) that will later post to a handler; also show a phone number and email as clearly marked SAMPLE placeholders (555-0142 and hello@summitlineroofing.example). FORBIDDEN CLAIMS: no invented statistics, years in business, job counts, star ratings or awards; no licence or insurance statements or licence numbers (none supplied or verified); no 'lifetime warranty' or any warranty terms; no 'best', '#1' or 'leading'; no guarantees about results or timing; no real customer names. PROOF section: use exactly three testimonials, each visibly labelled 'SAMPLE - replace with real customer feedback', with obviously fictional first-name-only attributions. PACKAGES section: three tiers named Repair, Replace and Care, each described by scope only; show NO dollar amounts (pricing display is an OPEN QUESTION, see below). OPEN QUESTIONS the build must not silently resolve (flag them on the page for a human, not as visible copy): (1) whether package prices should be shown, ranges or nothing, since the client's messages disagree; (2) which booking method is real, an online time-slot booking, a form that the office calls back on, or phone only, since the client has no booking tool and the phone is only answered in the mornings. Until answered, build the request form plus the phone number and do not imply a live calendar.
